title: Spend next year's money early

blocks.text: A water utility's board approves a new rule for its capital fund. A year may spend some of the next year's budget early, up to a share `max_advance` of that next year's budget, and whatever it spends early is no longer there to spend in the year it came from. A year may do both in one plan: lose part of its budget to the year before and spend early from the year after. The plan's last year has no next year to draw on. Money a year neither spends nor sends anywhere still lapses at year end. The model in `advance.py` still holds every year to its own budget, so it never uses the new rule.
The model so far, with $`Y`$ the plan's years in order, $`\text{spend}_y`$ the given linear expressions in the plan's 0/1 variables, and $`B_y`$ the budgets:

Your formulation replaces those rows. Write it first in this notation: each new variable with its domain and bounds, and each row with its quantifier and label. Then write `add_advances(model, spend, budgets, max_advance)` to add it, and return your new variables in a dict keyed by the year that spends early (the last year, which cannot borrow, has no entry). `add_yearly_budgets` shows the old rows; your function replaces them (the tests call yours alone).
The tests fix a plan and ask the solver whether it is allowed, so any correct formulation passes. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a plan that spends each year's budget exactly is allowed, and one that overspends a year by more than it may advance is refused
how much a year may advance is a share of the next year's budget, not its own
money spent early is no longer there to spend in the year it came from
the plan's last year has no next year to advance from
a plan that leaves money unspent is allowed
a middle year may have its money advanced to the year before and advance money from the year after in the same plan

origin.section: Unspent Money Lapses, So the Cash Row Is an Inequality

concepts: unspent money is a continuous variable that links each year's cash row to the next
money neither spent nor carried lapses, so the cash row is an inequality
